about.borders.body: The boundaries are simplified to roughly 200 metres. Within that distance of a border, a sensor can fall on the other side of the simplified line from the real one. Affected sensors are few and the effect on an area's median is smaller still, but a single sensor's area label near a province or district edge should not be treated as authoritative.
about.pollen.heading: Pollen is a model forecast, not a count
about.pollen.body: We do not measure pollen. The layer is the Copernicus CAMS European ensemble forecast for ragweed, mugwort, grasses, birch, alder and olive, in grains per cubic metre, delivered through Open-Meteo. We fetch it twice a day and show today and the next two days. An area takes the worst model cell inside it, or the nearest cell if none falls inside. A province shows the species with the highest level. The levels are low, moderate and high. Moderate starts at 10 grains per m³ for birch, alder, olive and mugwort and at 3 for grasses and ragweed. High starts at 100 and 50. These are the EAACI limits that CAMS uses. They are defined for hourly counts, and the map shows the daily mean forecast, so a day can read lower than the hourly scale would put it. No official Bulgarian numeric scale exists, so this is the European one.
about.bathing.heading: A bathing water class covers several seasons, not today
about.bathing.body: Bathing sites and classes come from the EEA WISE Bathing Water Directive tables, read through the Discodata API for Bulgaria, under CC BY 4.0. The class is calculated from E. coli and intestinal enterococci over the current season and the three before it. The EEA publishes once a year. We import weekly, and the map shows the newest classification for each site. Single samples in the site panel are context, not a verdict on the water today. The class does not cover chemical pollution.
about.borders.heading: A sensor near a border may be attributed to the neighbouring area
about.cities.body: For 13 of the 27 provincial capitals we use the boundary of the city itself. The other 14 have no settlement-level boundary in OpenStreetMap, so we use the boundary of the whole municipality instead. A municipality covers considerably more ground than its city: a sensor kilometres outside the built-up area (in a village, on a hillside, beside a road through farmland) is attributed to the city and moves its median. Rural air is usually cleaner in summer and, where solid fuel heating is common, dirtier in winter, so the bias is not in a fixed direction.
about.cities.heading: City areas are not all the same kind of thing
about.cities.list: Whole municipality: Blagoevgrad, Vratsa, Kardzhali, Lovech, Montana, Pazardzhik, Pernik, Pleven, Plovdiv, Sliven, Smolyan, Stara Zagora, Haskovo, Yambol.
about.cities.reading: So comparing Plovdiv (municipality) with Varna (city) compares two different kinds of area. The comparison is still informative. It is not like-for-like. Within one city the geometry is constant, so the trend over time is unaffected.
about.coverage.body: Sensor density varies enormously: Sofia has many, some provinces have very few. An area's figure is only as representative as the sensors inside it, and an area with two sensors is not measuring the same thing as an area with two hundred. That is why coverage state is shown alongside every figure instead of being folded invisibly into it. Check it before drawing a conclusion from a sparse area.
about.coverage.heading: Coverage is uneven, and reported rather than hidden
about.intro: This page covers what the map does not tell you on the page itself. Everything here is a property of the data rather than a bug waiting to be fixed, and each one can change how a number should be read.
about.privacy.heading: Privacy
about.privacy.storage_intro: It keeps a few preferences in your browser's local storage. They stay on your device. The site keeps no copy.
about.reference.body: The readings come from volunteer low-cost sensors, model forecasts and official EU classifications. They can be wrong, late or missing. Use them to stay aware, not to make health decisions. If you have symptoms or a condition, ask a doctor. For official alerts, follow the Ministry of Health, the regional health inspectorates (РЗИ) and the Executive Environment Agency (ИАОС).
about.reference.heading: This map is for reference, not medical advice
about.sensors.body: The readings come from the sensor.community network: low-cost optical particulate sensors, sited and maintained by volunteers. They are good at showing change over time and gross spatial patterns, and they are not regulatory monitors. High humidity in particular inflates optical PM readings. Their absolute values should not be compared against a legal limit as though they came from a reference station.
about.sensors.heading: The sensors are not reference instruments
about.sources.body: Readings from sensor.community contributors (ODbL 1.0). Province, city and Sofia district boundaries from OpenStreetMap (ODbL 1.0). The national boundary from Natural Earth. Pollen forecast from CAMS (Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service) via Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0). Bathing water classes from the European Environment Agency (CC BY 4.0).
about.sources.heading: Where the data comes from
about.title: About the data
about.page.title: About Kanarche
about.page.intro: A free, open map of the air in Bulgaria. Most readings come from sensors that volunteers run at home. The official stations of the Executive Environment Agency are shown alongside them.
about.toc.label: On this page
about.values.heading: What this project is
about.values.free.title: Free
about.values.free.body: No account, no paywall, no adverts. Every page works without signing in.
about.values.open.title: Open source
about.values.open.body: The code is on GitHub under the MIT licence.
about.values.community.title: Community driven
about.values.community.body: The citizen readings come from sensor.community volunteers. Anyone can report a problem or send a fix.
about.values.private.title: No personal data
about.values.private.body: No cookies, no analytics scripts, no accounts. We keep no IP address or identifier. Cloudflare, which delivers the site, does see your IP address, as any such network does.
about.values.phone.title: Made for phones
about.values.phone.body: Panels and charts are laid out for a small screen and work with a thumb.
about.goals.heading: What we are trying to do
about.goals.local.title: Show the air where you are
about.goals.local.body: Readings by neighbourhood, not one number for a whole city.
about.goals.honest.title: Be honest about what a number means
about.goals.honest.body: Coverage and caveats sit next to each figure. Low-cost sensors are indicative. They are not reference instruments.
about.goals.reuse.title: Make the data easy to reuse
about.goals.reuse.body: Every area has a page you can link to, and the map can be embedded on other sites.
about.start.heading: Getting started
about.start.intro: A short tour of what the map can do, grouped by what you want to do. Skim the headings or read it from the top.
about.start.layers.title: Choose what the map shows
about.start.layers.body: Open Layers to switch things on or off. Citizen sensors, official stations, wind and province outlines are on at first. Pollen, bathing water, inactive stations and faulty stations stay off until you ask for them.
about.start.layers.alt: The Layers menu open on the map, with the scale, cell values, citizen sensors, official stations, wind, pollen, bathing water, province outlines, inactive stations and faulty stations as checkboxes.
about.start.window.title: Look at now, or average over time
about.start.window.body: The map shows the latest readings, which citizen sensors send about every 5 minutes. Use the averaging period menu to see the average over the last 24 hours, 48 hours or week instead. An average is steadier, because one odd hour cannot swing it.
about.start.window.alt: The averaging period menu open on the map, with Now, Last 24 hours, Last 48 hours and Last week.
about.start.tilt.title: Tilt and turn the map
about.start.tilt.body: The Orientation button on the map, a small compass, opens a panel with Tilt and Heading sliders and a Reset to north button. Tilt goes up to 60 degrees. You can also right-drag or Ctrl+drag, or use two fingers on touch. Tilted, each hexagon rises into a column as tall as its reading, so the worst spots stand out.
about.start.tilt.alt: The map tilted over Sofia with hexagons raised into columns by their reading, and the Orientation panel open with the Tilt and Heading sliders and the Reset to north button.
about.start.areas.title: Follow your town or district
about.start.areas.body: Each province, provincial capital and Sofia district has its own page. Find them under the Areas tab at the top, next to Map and About. A page shows the median, the coverage and the last 24 hours.
about.start.areas.alt: The Plovdiv area page, with the current median, the number of sensors and the range over the last 24 hours.
about.start.embed.title: Put the map on your own site
about.start.embed.body: Copy one line of HTML to show the map on a school, municipal or news website. You can centre it on a province. There is nothing to install.
about.start.embed.alt: The map embedded on another page, centred on Plovdiv Province.
about.start.group.read.title: Read the map
about.start.group.find.title: Find your place
about.start.group.move.title: Move the map
about.start.group.layers.title: Extra layers
about.start.group.history.title: Look back
about.start.group.keep.title: Keep and share
about.start.metrics.title: Switch between measurements
about.start.metrics.body: Open the metric menu to choose PM2.5, PM10, temperature, humidity, pressure and, depending on the stations shown, gases and noise. Your choice stays in the link, so a shared link opens on the same measurement.
about.start.metrics.alt: The metric menu open on the map, listing PM2.5, PM10, temperature, humidity and the other measurements.
about.start.legend.title: Read the colours
about.start.legend.body: The Legend in the corner of the map unfolds into the colour key for the chosen measurement. Its "What the colours mean" link explains each band.
about.start.legend.alt: The legend unfolded in the corner of the map, with the colour scale and the "What the colours mean" link.
about.start.inactive.title: Show silent and faulty stations
about.start.inactive.body: A station is inactive when it has sent nothing for the chosen measurement in the last 2 hours, or 12 hours for official stations. It is faulty when at least half of its readings in the last 24 hours failed the quality checks, counting at least 6 readings. Both are hidden at first, because a map full of empty cells looks like an empty country and a faulty station has no usable value. Show them in Layers with "Inactive stations" and "Faulty stations".
about.start.inactive.alt: The Layers menu open on the map, with the "Inactive stations" and "Faulty stations" options ticked and the extra stations drawn on the map.
about.start.search.title: Jump to a place
about.start.search.body: Type a region, city, district or address in the search box. The map centres there, and an address gets a pin. Address search uses OpenStreetMap, where house numbers are patchy, so if nothing is found try the street name alone.
about.start.search.alt: The search box with suggestions for a city and its districts, and a pin on a searched address.
about.start.below.title: Scroll for the full picture
about.start.below.body: The arrows under the map lead to a second part of the page. There you find the median across provinces, the highest province figure, the provinces without data and a link to all areas.
about.start.below.alt: The bottom of the map with the down arrows, and below it the median across provinces and the highest province figure.
about.start.phone.title: Use it comfortably on a phone
about.start.phone.body: On a phone the buttons are sized for a finger, and one tap gives the map the whole screen. A sensor opens in a panel at the bottom. Scroll down for the readouts and charts.
about.start.phone.alt: Three phone screens: the map with its controls, a sensor panel open at the bottom, and the readouts and charts below the map.
about.start.pollen.title: See the pollen forecast
about.start.pollen.body: Switch on Pollen in Layers to colour the provinces by the forecast level for today and the next two days, then click a province to open its page. It is a model forecast, not a count.
about.start.pollen.alt: The map with the pollen layer on, provinces coloured from low to high, and the pollen forecast key in the corner.
about.start.sea.title: Check the bathing water
about.start.sea.body: Switch on Bathing water in Layers to see sea, lake and reservoir sites coloured by their EEA class, with E. coli and enterococci samples in the site panel. The class covers the last four seasons, so a single sample is context, not a verdict on the water today.
about.start.sea.alt: The Black Sea coast with bathing water sites coloured by class, and a site panel listing E. coli and enterococci samples.
about.start.wind.title: Watch the wind
about.start.wind.body: Moving particles show where the wind blows and how hard. Wind is on at first, and you can switch it off in Layers. Wind disperses pollution, and still air holds it in place.
about.start.wind.alt: The map with wind particles streaming across Bulgaria and the wind key in the corner.
about.start.official.title: See the official stations
about.start.official.body: The government monitoring stations are shown beside the citizen sensors, and you can hide or show them in Layers. They also bring nitrogen dioxide, ozone, sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide, benzene and noise. Their readings are older than citizen ones, so they count as inactive after 12 hours instead of 2.
about.start.official.alt: The map with official stations switched on and the metric menu showing the extra pollutants.
about.start.replay.title: Replay the past day or week
about.start.replay.body: Press play to watch the map change over the last 24 hours, 48 hours or week. A day plays hour by hour, two days in two-hour steps and a week in six-hour steps. Pick a speed from a quarter to double, and use the back button to return to the current readings.
about.start.replay.alt: The replay bar at the bottom of the map with the play button, the hour shown, the speed and the button back to the current readings.
about.start.charts.title: Chart a sensor over time
about.start.charts.body: Click a sensor to open its panel with a chart. Choose 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or 1 year, or set your own dates. Add the median, highest and lowest of the sensors nearby to see how yours compares.
about.start.charts.alt: A sensor panel with a line chart, the period selector and the nearby sensors median and range.
about.start.favourite.title: Keep one sensor close
about.start.favourite.body: Choose "Save as my sensor" in the sensor panel and the map opens on it next time. It is stored only in your browser.
about.start.favourite.alt: A sensor panel with the "Save as my sensor" button.
about.start.share.title: Share what you see
about.start.share.body: Open "More actions" in the sensor panel and choose Share. The link holds the sensor, the measurement and your choice of citizen and official stations. It does not hold the period or the map position.
about.start.share.alt: The "More actions" menu open in a sensor panel, with Share and Embed.
about.start.table.title: Read the provinces as a table
about.start.table.body: The Areas tab lists every province in a table. Filter by data, search by name and choose which columns to show.
about.start.table.alt: The Areas table with the filter, the search box and the Columns menu open above the list of provinces.
about.start.locate.title: Start from where you are
about.start.locate.body: Press Find me to centre the map near you. The first time, a small hint points to the button. The site remembers your last view, layers and period in your browser, and "Clear my settings" on this page forgets them.
about.start.locate.alt: The Find me button in the corner of the map with the hint "See the air near you" beside it.
about.privacy.intro: We keep no IP address or identifier: none in logs, none in the database. Your IP is used for a moment in memory to limit abusive traffic, then forgotten. Cloudflare, our network provider, sees it too and gives us only daily totals.
about.privacy.clear_note: Removes only the keys listed above.

about.visitors.intro: How many people open the site each day. The numbers come from Cloudflare's traffic totals. We run no counter in your browser.

about.involved.heading: Get involved
about.involved.body: Kanarche is open source and non-commercial. If you like it, a {repo} helps other people find it. Ideas for features and problem reports are welcome as {issues}.

home.about_pm: PM2.5 and PM10 are fine particles in the air, up to 2.5 and up to 10 microns across. Values are in µg/m³. Most readings come from volunteer sensors in the sensor.community network, and the official stations of the Executive Environment Agency are shown alongside. Colours follow the European Air Quality Index bands. For PM2.5, good is up to {good}, fair up to {fair}, moderate up to {moderate}, poor up to {poor}, very poor up to {verypoor}, and above that extremely poor.

The site loads no ads, tracking scripts or external fonts.

seo.terms.title: Terms of use and data disclaimer
seo.terms.description: How to read the data on Kanarche. It is indicative, comes with no warranty and is not for health decisions. Sources, licences and who we are not affiliated with.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: In short: the map is a free guide to the air in Bulgaria. It is not an official source and not medical advice.
terms.what.heading: What Kanarche is
terms.what.body: Kanarche (kanarche.eu) is a free map of the air in Bulgaria. It is non-commercial. There are no adverts, no paywall and no accounts. The source code is open under the MIT licence. Hosting is donated.
terms.sources.heading: Where the data comes from
terms.sources.intro: We do not measure anything ourselves. The map shows data that others collect and publish:
terms.sources.sc: citizen sensors on the Sensor.Community network, installed and looked after by volunteers
terms.sources.eea: official stations of the Executive Environment Agency (ИАОС), published through the European Environment Agency (EEA)
terms.sources.meteo: wind and pollen forecasts from Open-Meteo. The pollen forecast comes from the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS)
terms.sources.bathing: bathing water classes from the European Environment Agency
terms.sources.maps: the base map and boundaries from OpenStreetMap, and the national border from Natural Earth
terms.sources.body: Each source is responsible for the accuracy of its own data. We combine readings into area medians and averages. We run automatic quality checks and mark stations that fail them as faulty. We do not correct the values themselves.
terms.accuracy.heading: Treat the numbers as a guide
terms.accuracy.body: Citizen sensors are low-cost devices, not reference instruments. High humidity can push their readings up. Some stations may be old, poorly maintained or broken. We do not inspect, maintain or calibrate any station. Forecasts are models, not measurements. Any reading can be wrong, late or missing.
terms.health.body: Do not use this site for medical, health or safety decisions. If you have symptoms or a condition, ask a doctor. For official warnings, follow the Ministry of Health, the regional health inspectorates (РЗИ) and ИАОС.
terms.liability.heading: No warranty
terms.liability.body: We provide the site and the data as they are. We do not promise that they are accurate, complete, current or available at any given time. The site may change or stop without notice. To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any loss or damage that comes from using the site or the data, or from relying on them. This includes decisions made on the basis of what the map shows. Nothing here limits any liability that the law does not allow to be limited.
terms.affiliation.heading: Who we are not
terms.affiliation.body: Kanarche is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or run by Sensor.Community or airbg.info (Код България). It is also not affiliated with the Executive Environment Agency (ИАОС), the European Environment Agency, Copernicus, Open-Meteo or OpenStreetMap, nor with the Ministry of Health or the regional health inspectorates. We use their open data under their licences. Naming them credits the source. It does not mean they support or check this site.
terms.licences.heading: Licences
terms.licences.body: Each source keeps its own licence. We credit them on the map, in the footer and on the {licences} page. Sensor.Community data and OpenStreetMap data are under ODbL 1.0. Open-Meteo wind data, the CAMS pollen forecast and EEA bathing water data are under CC BY 4.0. ИАОС data published by the EEA follows the EEA terms of use. If you reuse data from this site, the original licence applies and you should credit the original source. The Kanarche code is under the MIT licence.
terms.privacy.heading: Privacy
terms.privacy.body: The site sets no cookies and keeps no IP address or other identifier. The details are on the {privacy} page and in the {about} section of About.
terms.contact.heading: Contact
terms.contact.body: Questions, corrections and problem reports are welcome as {issues} on GitHub. This is the only contact channel for now.
terms.changes.body: We may update these terms. The date at the top shows the last change. Every earlier version is in the public source code history.
